spec.title: TriviaQA — the same dataset, our worst QA cell against a healthy one
spec.held: the dataset (TriviaQA), the task shape (one short factual answer), and a comparable sample size (4,993 vs 4,392) and class balance (0.46 vs 0.48)
spec.varies: the model (OPT-30B base vs Qwen3-8B), the source cache, and the grader (ROUGE-L > 0.3 vs normalised exact match + judge)
spec.why: This is the pair Omri named first. Both cells answer the same benchmark at comparable n and comparable class balance, so neither sample size nor prevalence can explain the gap.
spec.note: The partner was changed after the Step-215 review. This pair originally used spilled_triviaqa_llama8b (0.9413) as the strong cell. That cell has 6 positives out of 256, trace_length alone scores 0.925 on it, and the project already carries a standing instruction to treat it as selection-biased and not headline it (scripts/advisor_report.py:783). Using it was an error: it inflated the gap to +37.99pp and every conclusion drawn from that pair. semenergy_triviaqa_qwen3_8b is the closest defensible control.

spec.title: GSM8K / Llama-3 — model size is the only variable
spec.held: the dataset (GSM8K), the source cache (the LapEigvals release), the decoding config, and the model family (Llama-3)
spec.varies: model size, 3B vs 8B — and nothing else
spec.why: The cleanest controlled comparison in the grid. If the feature quality moves here, it moves because of the model alone, with the data pipeline held fixed. This is the pair that can rule out a cache-specific artifact.

spec.title: K=10 multi-trace — the same pipeline, weak vs strong
spec.held: the K=10 multi-trace inference pipeline and its feature extraction
spec.varies: the dataset (MATH-500 vs GSM8K) and the model (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B vs Llama-3.1-8B)
spec.why: Both cells are built by the same multi-trace code, so a defect in that pipeline would hit both. It separates 'the K=10 path is broken' from 'this dataset/model is hard'.
